edition: Cosmic Encounter, FFG English CE01 original 2008, BGG 39463, original fifty aliens
verdict_basis: The complete base encounter procedure and all fifty alien-sheet abilities are substantially accurate. I found one limited but actionable rules omission concerning committing defender reward choices, plus a minor credit attribution issue. I found no major gameplay contradiction. Explicitly reported publisher ambiguities are not treated as invented rules or as automatic reasons to fail.

included: All fifty complete original printed alien sheets, inspected visually
Normal flare system and the summary's component-specific FAQ claims
Applicable base-only official FAQ answers through 2018, including answers embedded in mixed expansion sections
Retained May 6 2009 official errata not superseded by later answers
excluded: Reproduction of every individual flare/artifact card effect

findings.summary_ref: Actions > Attack against attack > Defense wins, defender rewards paragraph
findings.summary_quote: For each reward, draw one cosmic-deck card or retrieve one own warp ship to any own colony; combine these choices freely.
findings.issue: The summary does not say that the ally must declare all reward sources before taking any rewards. A reader could choose a deck draw, inspect it, then decide whether subsequent rewards should be more cards or warp ships.
findings.source_ref: Official FAQ through 2018 p8, Expansion-Specific Questions > Cosmic Incursion > Reward Deck
findings.source_quote: You must declare all of your reward sources before taking them.
findings.source_paraphrase: The answer requires stating the complete mix of ships and cards before collecting the rewards. Its example includes a warp ship and a cosmic-deck card as well as expansion reward-deck cards. The base-relevant commitment rule can be retained without introducing a reward deck.
findings.recommended_action: Add that each defensive ally declares the full mix of cosmic-deck draws and warp-ship retrievals before collecting any of those rewards.
findings.impact: Affects a limited reward-choice timing decision; the amounts, recipients and destinations in the summary are otherwise correct.

findings.summary_quote: Bill Eberle, Jack Kittredge, Bill Norton, Peter Olotka, Kevin Wilson
findings.issue: Kevin Wilson is listed under the designer field, whereas the supplied original rulebook credits him for Game Development.
findings.source_paraphrase: Game Design credits Bill Eberle, Jack Kittredge, Peter Olotka and Bill Norton. Game Development credits Kevin Wilson.
findings.recommended_action: Keep the four credited game designers in designer, and credit Kevin Wilson separately as developer if that metadata is desired.
findings.impact: Catalog metadata only; no effect on play.

core_rule_omissions.description: Declare the complete defender-reward source mix before taking rewards.

unresolved_authority.topic: When standard-game alien sheets first turn faceup
unresolved_authority.ruling_needed: The exact reveal point in ordinary setup after p6 directs players to place their chosen alien facedown.
sources_checked: 2008 rulebook p6 setup, p12 power loss, p14 Hidden Powers, complete rulebook and complete official FAQs
All fifty original alien sheets for any general setup override
unresolved_authority.evidence: The ordinary setup expressly places the chosen sheet facedown, but no later ordinary setup instruction expressly turns it faceup. Hidden Powers supplies a variant reveal rule, which cannot silently be imported into this excluded-variant scope.
unresolved_authority.summary_treatment: Accurately flags the missing ordinary reveal window rather than inventing one.
unresolved_authority.what_would_resolve: A publisher clarification or an edition-specific official corrected setup instruction stating the ordinary reveal point.
unresolved_authority.grade_effect: No contradiction charged solely for honestly recording this source gap.

unresolved_authority.topic: Reinforcement play when one or both revealed cards are negotiate
unresolved_authority.ruling_needed: Reconcile broad permission to play reinforcements on either side regardless of encounter-card types with the unqualified prohibition on playing one on a negotiate.
sources_checked: 2018 official FAQ p3 and p4, both native PDF page images and complete text
May 6 2009 official FAQ General Questions L93-L95
unresolved_authority.evidence: FAQ p3 permits involved players to play a reinforcement on either side regardless of the revealed encounter-card types. FAQ p4 asks whether a reinforcement can be played on a negotiate and answers No. The older FAQ only affirms playing on an attack side against negotiate; it does not reconcile the newer pair of answers.
unresolved_authority.summary_treatment: Faithfully records both statements and does not impose an unsupported harmonization.
unresolved_authority.what_would_resolve: Publisher clarification specifying whether the p4 answer concerns modifying the negotiate card itself, a particular side, or revokes part of the p3 permission.
unresolved_authority.grade_effect: No contradiction charged for transparently preserving this genuine conflict.

source_access_limitations.description: The historical official FAQ was supplied as a retained complete 573-line official webcache extraction because the native publisher PDF download returned HTTP 503. I read the entire retained extraction and used later 2018 answers wherever they supersede older ones. I did not independently obtain the historical PDF.

Every individual flare/artifact card is not among the assigned authoritative images. The summary explicitly delegates each card's effect/role/timing to its printed text. I verified the shared system, the two flare examples embedded in the rulebook, and all specific base FAQ claims it actually makes; I do not claim a complete visual audit of all individual flare/artifact cards.

checked_claim_groups.claims: Edition scope, 3-5 players, one-to-two-hour duration, colony definition, five foreign planets even in one system, alien precedence, original box counts and alternate Filch selection. No Anniversary-only components imported.

Twenty ships/five home planets/four ships each; unused destiny colors removed; secret two-flare alien choice; both dealt flares included; ten total flares; eight-card hands; private faces; first player destiny draw; printed restrictions and replacement procedure; alien setup instructions. Standard reveal gap honestly isolated.

Start Turn first encounter only; offense replacement before Regroup and Hate; optional playable cards before discard; defense replacement until encounter card; offense later encounter-card failure ends turn; all committed ships return to their own owners' existing colonies; no routine draw; successful deal differs from winning; second encounter requires an encounter card in primary hand.
Mandatory one-ship retrieval when available; existing colony destination; original no-colony gate exception and FAQ no-colonies/no-ships home-planet exception stated distinctly.

Shuffle final destiny card without drawing it; color/wild/special defense and system; own-color redraw/drive out/reclaim empty home planet; no ships of any color for automatic reclaim; win/success and Launch endpoint; hazard marks inert; all-defensive-planets occupied redraw.

One-to-four offense and ally ships from existing colonies; target-planet defense cannot change ships; zero-ship home defense; bystanders; colony stripping; no-ship encounters continue; offense invites first; response and commitment clockwise left of offense; no main-player alliance; physical defensive ally placement and FAQ considered-in-gate clarification.
Main players only select encounter cards; before/after timing preserved; simultaneous reveal with power exceptions; discard after resolution; normal victory at very end of Resolution.

All side ships plus main attack card; defense wins ties; precise winning/losing ship destinations; foreign-colony marker only for newly established colonies; defensive allies return to existing own colonies and receive one reward per contributed ship; base card-or-warp-ship choices. Reward commitment omission separately reported.

Negotiate loses against attack; own ships actually lost to warp determine compensation; no allied compensation; hand-card shortfall; random means unseen faces; prevented/eradicated losses ineligible; healing after warp arrival preserves eligibility; Human/Pacifist and original-reveal requirements preserved.

Allies return and gain nothing; one-minute deadline; cards from hands; at most one colony each where giver already has colony; non-warp ships may establish; coexistence/no vacancy; leftover gate ships return; at least one card/colony transfer; one-sided allowed; tangible terms restricted; future promises unenforceable; card terms truthful; failed deal each main player chooses three ships; turn consequence.

Single Morph; initial reveal copied before later changes; independent modifiers and Tripler examples; identity versus modified type/value split; normal post-resolution identity and discard; hypothetical double Morph losses.

Not encounter cards; artifacts follow their text and normally discard; Cosmic Zap use and rest-of-encounter duration; main players/allies may reinforce either side in Reveal and respond until all pass; no bystander eligibility. Conflicting negotiate FAQ wording remains unresolved.

Wild/Super identity rule; mandatory own Super if available; power loss/zap Wild access; immediate return after effect; one flare per player and one use per physical flare per encounter including changes of hands; cancellation counts versus prevented-play exception; Super-enabled power remains zappable; own Wild handoff exception.

Five current foreign colonies; marker decreases on loss; shared normal wins; end-of-Resolution window; explicit immediate wins and interrupts; alternate wins and Tick-Tock deal-created shared victory.

Immediate colony loss from last ship leaving; no return to abandoned colonies; relocation with no colonies goes to warp except explicit exceptions; extra-loss chooser; outside-encounter cost restriction; controlled ships; sent/lost/losing distinctions and interrupted arrival.

Fewer-than-three home colonies; immediate lost power and identity; restoration; Masochist exception; bold-italic use; non-use clauses remain; no preemptive zap; immediate same-phase window; offense/defense/clockwise order; unassociated effects last; complete one effect except interrupts; optional effects may change mind; once per relevant context.

Public hand size and discards; no hand showing without effect; public table talk; ordinary bluff claims versus Mind/deal restrictions; ordered discards; terminology; legal encounter; Mobius no-colony destinations; six base card types; cosmic-deck recycling, Cosmic Quake and Aftershock including Miser hoard.

Each complete printed power, setup instruction, restriction, quantitative threshold/cost, actor, destination, exception, optional/mandatory label and phase strip inspected against the corresponding summary entry. Macron, Spiff, Warrior, Mind Wild and Reincarnator Wild use retained errata; Will uses current Destiny correction. Individual receipts and coverage below.

completeness.source_texts: Complete contiguous text delivered, including document tails; native text of both PDFs matches the supplied extractions after removing page wrappers and whitespace.
completeness.alien_sheets: All fifty original_file images inspected in full at native 663x1000; every image explicitly forwarded with original detail. Actual returned base64-decoded JPEG payload hashes independently equal pinned original SHA-256 values.
completeness.summary_claims: All summary sections and all fifty individual alien entries reconciled to assigned sources. No question-based accuracy inference used.
completeness.core_rules: Substantially complete; one limited source-backed defender-reward timing omission.
completeness.source_authority: Complete assigned modern PDFs and fifty sheets available; historical native PDF unavailable but accepted retained official extraction read in full; two genuine unresolved publisher issues documented.
